info.title: Redmine MCP REST API
info.description: REST data plane for a self-hosted Redmine: issues, projects, users, time entries, wiki, versions, categories, memberships, relations, enumerations and search, plus the gated writes. Reads exist so a shell-capable client can curl | jq bulk payloads without them crossing the LLM context window, and every read also accepts format=text to get the same markdown the MCP tool renders. Writes are validated with the MCP tools own exported Zod schemas, so the two surfaces cannot drift. Two things to know before relying on this: Redmine marks only Issues, Projects, Users, Time Entries and News as Stable, and the wiki, version, membership, relation, category, enumeration, custom-field and search endpoints as Alpha, so they may change between releases; and every collection caps at limit=100 server side, which is why each list answers { items, page } with the window it returned. The deletes, project archiving and the project/version/category/membership admin creates are deliberately NOT exposed here — Redmine has no recycle bin, a project delete cascades into its subprojects, and a curl has no confirmation affordance.

get.summary: Search and filter Redmine issues
get.description: One page of issues with the total reported. Multi-valued filters go upstream as ONE comma-joined parameter (issueIds=1,2,3) because repeated keys are silently ignored. Custom-field filters are passed as `cf_<id>` query keys, e.g. ?cf_3=Urgent, with IDs from the custom-fields endpoint. Anything that is not `cf_<digits>` is dropped rather than forwarded, because Redmine silently ignores an unknown filter — which widens the result set and reads as "the filter matched everything". Mirrors the MCP tool `listIssues`.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Restrict to one project (ID or identifier). Omit to search every visible project.

parameters.name: subprojectId
parameters.description: Subproject filter. Pass !* to EXCLUDE subprojects.

parameters.name: trackerId
parameters.description: Tracker ID from the trackers endpoint.

parameters.name: statusId
parameters.description: open (Redmine default), closed, * for any, or a numeric status ID.

parameters.name: assignedToId
parameters.description: Assignee user ID, or the literal "me".

parameters.name: authorId
parameters.description: Author user ID, or "me".

parameters.name: parentId
parameters.description: Return only subtasks of this issue.

parameters.name: issueIds
parameters.description: Comma-separated issue IDs.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Subject filter. Prefix with ~ for "contains"; a bare string matches exactly.

parameters.name: createdOn
parameters.description: Creation-date filter in Redmine operator syntax, e.g. >=2026-01-01 or ><2026-01-01|2026-03-31.

parameters.name: updatedOn
parameters.description: Last-updated filter, same syntax as createdOn.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column; append :desc to reverse, e.g. updated_on:desc.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: Associations to embed in each issue.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Records to skip. The response `page` reports the window that came back.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Records per page. Redmine caps this at 100 server-side and silently returns 100 for anything larger, so values above it are rejected here instead.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Response shape. Defaults to the { items, page } JSON envelope (or the raw record for a by-ID read); text/plain/markdown render the same output the MCP tool returns. Accept: text/plain does the same thing.

parameters.name: cf_<id>
parameters.description: Custom-field filter, e.g. ?cf_3=Urgent, with IDs from the custom-fields endpoint. Keys that are not cf_<digits> are ignored. A cf_<digits> key given more than once is REJECTED with 400 rather than dropped: Redmine answers a missing filter with more rows, so a silent drop would return a wider result set than was asked for. Pass multiple values comma-joined (?cf_3=a,b).

200.description: Issues for the requested window, as { items, page } — `page` carries total_count, offset and limit. Follow it before treating the list as complete.

400.description: Query parameters failed the MCP tool schema, or a cf_<digits> filter was given more than once. `issues` carries the flattened Zod field errors; `invalidKeys` names the unusable custom-field keys.

401.description: Missing or invalid bearer token for THIS API. A rejected Redmine credential answers 502, not 401 — see that response.

403.description: No Redmine connection on the account, the connection has no instance URL, or Redmine denied the call (a missing permission, or an administrator-only endpoint).

404.description: Record not found. Redmine also answers 404 for records the account is not allowed to see.

422.description: Redmine rejected the values. The message carries Redmine own `errors` list.

502.description: The Redmine instance was unreachable, redirected the request away from the configured host, or rejected the stored credential. The request to this API was authenticated; the upstream call was not.

post.description: Only projectId and subject are required; every other field falls back to the project or tracker default. Accepts a body up to 5 MB, since `description` is a full issue body. Mirrors the MCP tool `createIssue`.

post.summary: Update a Redmine issue or append a comment
post.description: POST rather than PUT because this catalog method union is GET and POST; Redmine itself takes a PUT here. `notes` APPENDS a comment while `description` REPLACES the body — fields left out are untouched. A body that changes nothing is rejected with 400 rather than sent. Accepts up to 5 MB. Redmine answers the write with 204 and no body, so the issue is re-read and returned. Mirrors the MCP tool `updateIssue`.

parameters.description: Issue ID. Wins over any issueId in the body.

post.summary: Create or replace a Redmine wiki page
post.description: The clearest large-body case on this plane: `text` REPLACES the entire page, so read the page first if you mean to edit rather than overwrite. Accepts up to 5 MB. A title that does not exist yet is created — Redmine uses one endpoint for both. Pass `version` for optimistic locking so a concurrent edit is rejected instead of clobbered. The page is re-read afterwards, which is also how you get the new version number the next locked write needs. Mirrors the MCP tool `updateWikiPage`.

parameters.description: Project numeric ID or URL identifier (the slug in the project URL). Redmine accepts either everywhere.

post.description: Provide issueId OR projectId. Most instances require activityId — the time-entry-activities endpoint lists them. NOT idempotent: a retried request logs the hours twice. Mirrors the MCP tool `createTimeEntry`.

201.description: Redmine { time_entry } payload for the created entry.

400.description: Query or body parameters failed the MCP tool schema. `issues` carries the flattened Zod field errors. Redmine silently ignores filters it does not recognise, so these are rejected here rather than forwarded.

401.description: Missing or invalid bearer token for THIS API. A rejected Redmine credential answers 502, not 401 — see that response.

403.description: No Redmine connection on the account, the connection has no instance URL, or Redmine denied the call (a missing permission, or an administrator-only endpoint).

404.description: Record not found. Redmine also answers 404 for records the account is not allowed to see.

422.description: Redmine rejected the values. The message carries Redmine own `errors` list.

502.description: The Redmine instance was unreachable, redirected the request away from the configured host, or rejected the stored credential. The request to this API was authenticated; the upstream call was not.

get.summary: Full text search across Redmine
get.description: q is required. The record-type toggles are PRESENCE flags upstream, so passing one as false is the same as leaving it out. Alpha upstream. Mirrors the MCP tool `searchRedmine`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search terms. Required. ?query= is accepted as an alias, since that is the MCP parameter name.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Restrict the search to one project. Omit to search everything visible.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Breadth of the search. subprojects only means anything alongside projectId.

parameters.name: titlesOnly
parameters.description: Match titles only instead of full text.

parameters.name: issues
parameters.description: Include issues.

parameters.name: news
parameters.description: Include news entries.

parameters.name: documents
parameters.description: Include documents.

parameters.name: wikiPages
parameters.description: Include wiki pages.

parameters.name: openIssues
parameters.description: Restrict issue hits to open issues.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Records to skip. The response `page` reports the window that came back.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Records per page. Redmine caps this at 100 server-side and silently returns 100 for anything larger, so values above it are rejected here instead.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Response shape. Defaults to the { items, page } JSON envelope (or the raw record for a by-ID read); text/plain/markdown render the same output the MCP tool returns. Accept: text/plain does the same thing.

200.description: Search results for the requested window, as { items, page } — `page` carries total_count, offset and limit. Follow it before treating the list as complete.

bearerAuth.description: Bearer token from the mintRestBearerForCurl MCP tool (5-minute TTL) or a permanent dashboard API key.

issues.description: Present on 400 only: the flattened Zod error ({formErrors, fieldErrors}).

invalidKeys.description: Custom-field query keys that could not be used, when that is why the request was rejected.

Pagination.description: The window Redmine actually returned. total_count is the full match count; offset is where to resume.

ObjectResponse.description: Redmine own single-record envelope, keyed by the resource name (issue, project, user, wiki_page, version, time_entry).

id.description: Custom field ID from the custom-fields endpoint.

projectId.description: Project numeric ID or URL identifier.

description.description: Issue body, in the markup the instance is configured for. This is the field the 5 MB body limit exists for.

statusId.description: Omit to use the tracker default.

parentIssueId.description: Create this as a subtask of that issue.

UpdateIssueRequest.description: Every field is optional, but a body that changes nothing is rejected with 400 rather than sent. The issueId in the path wins over one here.

description.description: REPLACES the issue body. Use `notes` to add a comment without touching it.

notes.description: APPENDS a comment to the issue history.

statusId.description: Read the issue with include=allowed_statuses to see which transitions are legal.

CreateTimeEntryRequest.description: Provide issueId OR projectId; a body with neither is rejected with 400 rather than spending a 422 round-trip.

spentOn.description: Defaults to today on the Redmine side.

activityId.description: Required unless the instance has a default.

userId.description: Log on behalf of another user. Needs the log-time-for-other-users permission.

UpdateWikiPageRequest.description: projectId and title come from the path and win over the same keys here.

text.description: Full page body. REPLACES the existing content entirely — this is the field the 5 MB body limit exists for.

parentTitle.description: Title of the parent wiki page, to nest this one under it.

version.description: Version being edited, for optimistic locking. A mismatch is rejected by Redmine instead of clobbering a concurrent edit.
